chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the woman for whom a shade is established and she is in Ihraam. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So the man upon whom a shade is struck and he is in Ihraam?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when he has a headache, and he would give in charity with one Mudd for each day'.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الظِّلَالُ: Shade (used here to denote protection from sun/heat)
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A traditional unit of volume for dry food, approximately 750 grams

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for using shade while in Ihraam due to a headache?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that the permissibility of using shade (*al-zilal*) for a person in *Ihraam* due to a headache (*shaqiqah*) applies equally to men and women, provided they compensate with one *Mudd* of food per day. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (*rukhas*) in pilgrimage rituals, linking physical relief to specific charitable obligations to maintain the sanctity of the state of consecration.
